summary: Conservation is central to Gabon’s pledges: net absorption is projected at -79.4 MtCO₂ eq in 2030 and -92.4 MtCO₂ eq from 2035 under existing measures, reaching -94.9 and -121.5 MtCO₂ eq in 2030/2035 with support; removals could improve by up to 108% versus BAU. Gabon targets 2,000 ha under conservation status, 21% protected territory and 30% ecosystem protection by 2030; mixed land-use measures place 60% of territory in sustainable forestry concessions, while maintaining net removals of at least 100 million tCO₂ eq/year beyond 2050. Restoration includes 10,000 ha of degraded-forest reforestation and rehabilitation of eight landfills. Agriculture includes 700 ha of shade coffee (140 ha annually), 2 ha of cacao annually, five composting platforms and a possible 50% cut in per-hectare emissions. With forest at 91.5% and agriculture at 4.0%, the 10,000-ha restoration target is about 0.04% of forest; 700 ha of coffee is about 0.07% of agriculture.
